$description: Tier 1 · Global primitives. Raw values only. Emitted as --g-*. Never referenced by components directly; semantic tokens alias these. Deprecated since 1.1 (Unicron 7): the neutral ramp (--g-neutral-*), the accent ramps (--g-blue-*, --g-coral-*, --g-green-*, --g-amber-*, --g-red-*) and white-alpha. They stay, unchanged, for all of 1.x, because app layers alias them; 2.0 removes them, once no app reads them (docs/02-tokens.md → Deprecated). No core role points at the neutral ramp; success, warning and info still read their accent steps, which 2.0 moves to status-named tokens. The hue angles stay.

hue.$description: Bare hue angles for tinted surfaces. Lightness and chroma are semantic, so one hue gives a pastel wash in light mode and a deep one in dark.

theme.$description: Theme slots: the 10 values a theme sets, the accent only (Unicron 2.0): primary fill, the label on it, primary as text, the soft wash and primary as large type, per ground (graphite = dark, stone = light). Everything else (surfaces, inks, lines, status, counts, labels, charts) is shared by every app and lives in `base` below, because the apps look the same and only their accent differs (Sean, 2026-11-23). These hold Unicron's own default accent, a quiet slate blue. No app's theme lives in the core (Unicron 1): an app declares these 10 in its own layer, `[data-theme="<app>"] { --g-theme-…: …; }`, and measures them with `unicron-contrast`. Figma has no Default mode: the Warpcore, Vale, Lockdown, Synapse and Fontface modes of Unicron / Theme differ only in these five roles.

base.$description: Unicron 2.0's shared neutrals and signals: one value per ground, the same in every app and in every one of Figma's 10 modes of Unicron / Theme (read 2026-11-24 from the published library, file nmLJwY8cugquuZqs8xyZr9). Surfaces step 2–4% apart (sunken, ground, raised, popover); lines, hover and selection are the body ink at a low alpha so they work on any layer. Tier 2 reads the stone value in light and the graphite value in dark.

surface-ground.$description: Figma surface/ground. The page: the main content and the chat.

surface-sunken.$description: Figma surface/sunken. Window edge and sidebar, a step below surface/ground.

surface-raised.$description: Figma surface/raised. Cards, the right panel, the composer. On stone it equals the ground; a hairline separates them.

surface-popover.$description: Figma surface/popover. Menus, popovers, dialogs: the only layer with a shadow.

surface-popover-frost.$description: Figma surface/popover-frost. Frosted menus and floating bars (Sean, 2026-11-23: frosted glass is the default for menus): the popover at 72%, under a 24px backdrop blur.

surface-hover.$description: Figma surface/hover. A row or quiet button under the pointer: the body ink at 5%.

surface-selected.$description: Figma surface/selected. A selected or pressed row, pill, chip or segment: the body ink at 8%.

line-rule.$description: Figma line/rule. Hairlines and 1px borders: the body ink at 8%.

line-strong.$description: Figma line/strong. Inputs, scrollbar thumbs and a stronger hairline: the body ink at 14%.

line-field.$description: Figma line/field. A field's resting border: the body ink at 14%, as Figma draws it. Below 3:1 by design (Unicron 2.0); focus draws line-focus.

line-grid-dot.$description: Figma line/grid-dot. The dot grid and the sheet grabber: the body ink at 14%.

swatch.$description: Twelve colours for things a person colours: calendars, notes, labels, personas, graph kinds (contract 5.1b #55). Evenly spaced OKLCH hues 30° apart, starting at the system's red hue angle (hue.red, 25). Each is solved per ground, the same for every app: the lightness that holds APCA Lc 62 (60, the floor for coloured text, plus 2) against the lowest-contrast of the eight surfaces it can sit on (surface-ground and surface-raised in all four apps), at a chroma of 0.14 on stone and 0.13 on graphite, or less where sRGB has no room at that lightness. So a swatch holds as text, and as a 2px bar, edge or mark (Lc 30) with room to spare. A swatch is a colour for data, never a status; it is never a fill behind text. Not in Figma.

scrim.$description: The full-screen dim behind sheets, dialogs and menus (Figma surface/scrim, VariableID:54:50), the same for every app. Graphite is opaque black; stone carries 64% alpha inside the colour, as Figma stores it. The layer's own opacity is a tier 3 knob (--c-scrim-sheet, -dialog, -menu): 0.5, 0.6 and 0.32 on graphite, 1 on stone, where this 64% is the whole dim.

graphite.$description: Figma surface/scrim (VariableID:54:50) in every graphite mode.

stone.$description: Figma surface/scrim (VariableID:54:50) in every stone mode: #141618 at 64% alpha.

radius.$description: The radius scale (Figma Space collection, radius/*). Corners grow with the size of the thing: 4 checkbox and keycap, 6 controls, 8 menus and rows, 12 cards and panels, 16 the composer, round for pills, dots and avatars.

xs.$description: 4px: Figma radius/xs. Checkbox, keycap, inline code.

control.$description: 6px: Figma radius/control (VariableID:7:31). Buttons, inputs, pill tabs.

md.$description: 8px: Figma radius/md. Menus, rows, small cards, option cards.

lg.$description: 12px: Figma radius/lg. Cards, banners, dialogs, a floating panel.

xl.$description: 16px: Figma radius/xl. The composer and the user's message bubble.

round.$description: Figma radius/round (VariableID:7:32). Pills, chips, dots, avatars, the send button.

size.$description: Control and icon sizes Figma holds as variables (Space collection). Every other fixed size is a tier 3 knob of the component that draws it.

control.$description: 48px: Figma size/control (VariableID:27:1982). Every floating control, the tab bar, the status strip, a text field's least height.

touch-min.$description: 44px: Figma size/touch-min (VariableID:27:1983). The floor for a touch target.

control-s.$description: 28px: Figma size/control-s. Small buttons, pill tabs, filter chips, header icon buttons.

control-m.$description: 32px: Figma size/control-m. Buttons, text fields, menu rows, sidebar rows.

control-l.$description: 44px: Figma size/control-l (an alias of size/touch-min). Sheet buttons, stacked full width.

icon.$description: 20px: Figma size/icon. Material Symbols Rounded at opsz 20.

check.$description: A checkbox and a radio: 20px (Figma size/check).

track.$description: A progress track and a thin bar: 4px (Figma size/track).

field-text-touch.$description: A field's text size on a touch screen: iOS zooms the page into a focused field set under 16px. Not in Figma: a platform floor, not a style (Unicron 2.0, where body went to 15px).

stroke.$description: The two stroke widths the direction draws. Figma types them in; it has no stroke variable.

emphasis.$description: Focus and error borders, the selected-row edge, the tab indicator.

press.$description: A control going down under a finger or a click. The one step under 120ms: the hand is already there, so it must feel immediate.

state.$description: A surface changing state: a panel opening, a selection moving to a new place.

move.$description: Travel across the screen. The ceiling: no default motion runs longer.

tick.$description: One step of a countdown ring: a second, run linear, so the ring tracks the clock.

spin.$description: One turn of a spinner or a working ring.

pulse.$description: One beat of a pulse or a breathing halo: slow enough to read as alive, not alarming.

out.$description: Ease-out cubic: quick start, soft landing. Softer than standard.

in.$description: Ease-in cubic: slow start, fast finish. For things leaving.

in-out.$description: Ease-in-out cubic: for travel from one resting place to another.

back.$description: Overshoots to about 112% and comes back. For rare moments only.

pulse.$description: The even in-and-out of a pulse loop.

spring.$description: Damped springs at mass 1. Built to a CSS linear() curve that runs over the matching -duration token; the raw stiffness and damping are kept in tokens.json for JS. Each duration is the time the spring takes to stay within 1% of rest (scripts/check.mjs holds the two together).

settle.$description: A small thing arriving at a new place, with a slight overshoot (about 8%).

firm.$description: A large surface arriving. Under 3% overshoot, so it reads as physical with no visible bounce.

pop.$description: A clear bounce (about 20%). Expressive only: no core role points here.

step.$description: The delay between one sibling starting and the next.

max.$description: Siblings after this many start together, so the last one still lands inside the ceiling (4 steps of 50ms, then a 200ms entrance, is 400ms).

depth.$description: Scale of a pressed control of ordinary size (4% smaller).

depth-small.$description: Scale of a pressed icon-size control (10% smaller): a small target needs a larger change to show.

font.$description: Geist and Geist Mono, as values. @unicron/ui loads the font files (@fontsource-variable/geist, @fontsource-variable/geist-mono); the plain family name follows for an app that installs the static fonts.

elevation.$description: Shadows for things that float, and only those (Figma effect styles Unicron Elevation/*): menus, popovers, tooltips, dialogs, the phone sheet and the floating tab bar. Panels and cards take a hairline, no shadow.

blur.$description: The backdrop blur under a frosted surface (Figma Unicron Elevation/popover's background blur).
